Jonas,

Attached is our legal team's redline of the MSA focusing on the indemnity and third-party claim sections. Two items they flagged as non-starters for Acme:

- Redwood's proposed customer indemnity for third-party IP claims that contain a broad assignment of liability (they'd like limits around claims arising from customer content vs. Redwood-delivered software).

1) You can add a carve-out for claims caused primarily by Customer modifications or Customer-provided content;
2) Redwood will agree to a notice-and-cooperation flow, and whether Redwood requires first notice within 30 days of claim receipt (Acme prefers 14 days).

I'm cc'ing our procurement lead and legal counsel. We also attached the Order Form with the customer-specified SOW reference (Exhibit A).

Jonas / Carlos — I reviewed Acme's redline and drafted suggested language (attached) that preserves Redwood's ability to control defenses for IP infringement claims while addressing Acme's concerns. Key points in our suggested compromise:  

1) Mutuality on customer-provided content: Redwood will not seek indemnity for claims caused primarily by Customer data, Customer modifications, or Customer-provided third-party components.
2) Notice and cooperation: Customer must provide prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation; we agree to a 14-day notice window where practicable but cannot make it an absolute condition for indemnity (we propose: prompt notice and commercial reasonableness).
3) Control of defense & settlement: Redwood will have the right to assume control of the defense with counsel of its choice for IP claims, provided that Redwood obtains Customer's written consent for any settlement that would materially affect Customer's rights or require payment by Customer.
4) Cap and consequential damages: We propose no unlimited exposure for Redwood on indemnity; instead, Redwood suggests a dedicated IP indemnity cap tied to the Order Form value (e.g., 12 months of fees) or an explicit $1,000,000 cap for this account.

Attached: Redlines_Response_MSA.docx (tracks proposed edits and rationale). If Acme prefers we can map the cap to Exhibit A/Order Form.

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Mina/Jonas — thanks for the proposed language. A couple of items from Acme counsel:  

- Acme will accept Redwood controlling the defense for IP claims only if Redwood agrees to (i) use counsel with relevant expertise (we list preferred firms in our vendor guide), and (ii) include a 30-day cure period for claims tied to Customer configuration changes.
- The $1,000,000 flat cap is acceptable as a starting point for discussion, but Acme would like express confirmation that open-source component claims and third-party patent assertions tied to Customer modifications remain the Customer's responsibility.
- Regarding notice: Acme insists on a 14-day written notice after the customer first receives a claim or reasonably should have known — otherwise Acme reserves the right to assume defence.

We attached our counter redline and included annotated examples where the language needs clarification. Can Redwood confirm acceptance of counsel standards and the 30-day cure window? If not, please propose alternate language that we can present internally.

Regards,
Acme Legal

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — final proposal and next step (DocuSign ready)

Acme / Carlos / Legal team — thanks for the thoughtful counter. After internal alignment with Mina and product/legal leadership, here's a pragmatic compromise we can accept to close the loop:  

- Carve-out: Mutual carve-out for claims caused primarily by Customer data, Customer modifications, or Customer-provided third-party components. Redwood will not indemnify such claims.
- Defence control: Redwood will assume control of defence for IP infringement claims and will retain counsel with relevant IP experience. Redwood will allow Customer to approve any settlement that (a) imposes payment obligations on Customer or (b) materially affects Customer's rights; Redwood will not unreasonably withhold such approval.
- Cure window: We can live with a 30-day technical cure window tied to claims arising from Customer configuration changes, provided the Customer gives prompt written notice and cooperation.
- Notice: We accept Acme's 14-day notice preference as an objective expectation but will phrase the clause as prompt written notice combined with a 14-day target where practicable to avoid forfeiture for minor delays beyond Customer control.
- Cap: Redwood proposes an IP indemnity cap of the greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form (Exhibit A). This ties risk to the economic value of the engagement.

If Acme agrees to the above, we will update the MSA/Order Form (Exhibit A) and send a DocuSign packet. I've attached the Order Form reference for clarity. Proposed next steps:  
1) Acme legal to confirm acceptance or provide one narrow redline on settlement approval language.
2) If accepted, we will prepare DocuSign and route for signatures (HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345).
3) If Acme wants a quick alignment call, set 30 minutes — otherwise we'll proceed to signatures.

Link to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABC-ACME-2025

Thanks — appreciate the collaboration.

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
